h: A Night in the Harbour City
p: Bristol is a city of many layers, and an evening at the lanes is easily the cherry on top of a day of exploring. The Harbourside is the obvious starting point. Brunel's SS Great Britain sits in its dry dock there, and it's one of the city's best attractions for history lovers. Along the water, M Shed tells the story of Bristol and its people, and We The Curious is a hands-on science centre that's brilliant for families.

Up the hill, Clifton Suspension Bridge spans the Avon Gorge and makes for an unforgettable view. Cabot Tower on Brandon Hill offers another lookout over the rooftops. Street art fans can spend hours hunting down murals, as Bristol's walls have become famous for their creativity. Stokes Croft is one area well known for it.
With a busy city all around, make sure you get the logistics right. Bristol Temple Meads is the main station, and the city centre is walkable, though it's fairly hilly in places.

At the lanes, a little preparation goes a long way. Pick a ball you can control rather than the heaviest on the rack, aim for the arrows on the lane instead of staring at the pins, and follow through. If there are first-timers in your group, mix them into teams with a stronger bowler to keep things fair. And keep track of the time so the food order goes in before the hunger kicks in.
